correctness.rationale: The proof explicitly derives the coefficients by Lagrange evaluation at zero, proves strict growth of \(|c_j|/N_j\) for every strict integer-divisibility chain, and shows midpoint sets overlap if and only if their integer refinement ratio is odd. This partitions all distinct sampled nodes into disjoint blocks whose alternating weight tails have the last coefficient sign, proving necessity and sufficiency. Summing negative blocks yields exact negative mass, constant exactness yields the sharp norm, and the final new nodes give the maximum weight. Midpoint Euler–Maclaurin with polynomial remainder zero proves degree \(2d+1\). Standard-library exact-rational verification passed on 680 chains and 5 full-order examples; these checks corroborate rather than substitute for proof.

originality.rationale: The compared 2014 Farzi paper and the entire 2026-09-21 and 2026-10-13 published quadrature RESULT texts concern composite trapezoidal grids. Berrut–Trummer 2022 supplies the midpoint-offset setting but not the exact all-chain physical-node parity/sign theorem. These references already cover the Richardson coefficients and much of the alternating-magnitude technique, so novelty is confined to midpoint-grid block geometry, the parity classification, its negative mass and noise norm. Full text for the 2022 de Camargo classical Romberg result and the older Sidi article was not accessible; historical priority is provisional.

Sidi 1997 generalized Richardson article was not fully inspected, so an implicit physical-node sign specialization cannot be ruled out absolutely.
Older generalized midpoint-extrapolation books and unpublished notes may contain the same exact parity criterion under other terminology.
Semantic database search and own-ledger partition cannot prove global uniqueness.

value.rationale: Positive collected quadrature weights ensure nonnegative sampled data cannot yield a negative estimate and give the least possible bounded absolute-sample-noise norm. Midpoint grids have a nontrivial parity-dependent overlap that makes an extrapolation chain either positive or negative despite the same order of polynomial exactness. The universal if-and-only-if parity rule and exact failure cost allow selection of admissible mixed integer-refinement chains, a natural numerical quadrature design problem rather than a routine coefficient substitution.
